The sample


Our sample is taken from the Corporate Library (now GMI Ratings) and Audit Analytics databases for the


period 2001-2011. Table 1 gives the sample selection details.

Firms for which both the gender of the directors and other corporate board characteristics (required for


CGboard and CEOpower variables) are available from Corporate Library are first selected. Out of these, the firms


for which the audit fee data are available from the Audit Analytics database are retained in the sample. Further, the


audit fee model requires financial data. After eliminating firms with missing data, 9,392 firm-year observations are


left for our analysis.


Of the 9,392 firm years, <mark>6,639 observations have one or more female directors (</mark> <mark>FDir</mark> <mark>= 1) whereas 2,753</mark>


<mark>observations have no female directors (</mark> <mark>FDir</mark> <mark>= 0). Thus, the matching procedure results in some of the all-male</mark>


<mark>boards in the sample being used twice. We find the closest propensity score match for each of the firms with</mark>


<mark>female director(s) and then eliminate the pair if the difference in their propensity scores is greater than 0.001. The</mark>


<mark>elimination of dissimilar pairs leaves 2,884 propensity score matched pairs, or a total of 5,768 observations. For</mark>


<mark>the propensity score matching for female audit committee members, there are 3,998 firms with female audit</mark>


<mark>committee members (</mark> <mark>FAud</mark> <mark>= 1) that are matched with firms without female audit committee members (</mark> <mark>FAud</mark> <mark>= 0).</mark>


<mark>To be consistent with the matching procedure that we used for</mark> <mark>FDir</mark> <mark>, we match firms with at least one female audit</mark>


<mark>committee member with those that have no female audit committee members. Unlike the matching procedure for</mark>


<mark>gender-diverse boards, this process results in the elimination of some of the all-male audit committees. After</mark>


<mark>removal of pairs with propensity scores differences that are greater than 0.001, 1,495 propensity score matched</mark>


<mark>pairs for a total of 2,990 firm-year observations remain.</mark>


Table 2 (panel A) compares boards with female directors to all-male boards that are propensity score


matched. The p -values for t -tests of the difference between means and medians of the two subsamples are shown


in the last two columns. The average audit fee is significantly higher in the subsample with female directors than in


the subsample with all-male directors. Panel B compares the audit committee with female directors to propensity


score matched all-male committees. Consistent with our expectation, the average audit fee is higher for the


subsample with female audit committee members.
